module.aws_eks_self_managed_node_groups:resource.aws_autoscaling_group.self_managed_ng: explicit depends_on of module.aws_eks_self_managed_node_groups:resource.aws_iam_role.self_managed_ng is redundant — already implied by attribute references
The explicit depends_on on aws_iam_role.managed_ng is redundant because node_role_arn already references aws_iam_role.managed_ng[0].arn, which establishes the same dependency implicitly.
The explicit depends_on on aws_iam_role.emr_on_eks_execution is redundant because the local-exec command already references aws_iam_role.emr_on_eks_execution.id.
The explicit depends_on on kubernetes_namespace.spark is redundant because the local-exec command already references kubernetes_namespace.spark.id.

The aws_eks_teams module creates Kubernetes namespaces, RBAC resources, and manifests but has no ordering dependency on the aws-auth ConfigMap or cluster readiness. Its Kubernetes resources can race with cluster/API readiness; add depends_on = [kubernetes_config_map.aws_auth] so they are created only after read-readiness and aws-auth are applied.

The ClusterRoleBinding's role_ref.name is a literal string instead of a reference to kubernetes_cluster_role.team, so Terraform does not order the binding after the ClusterRole. It can be applied before the role exists.
The RoleBinding's role_ref.name is a literal string instead of a reference to kubernetes_role.team, so Terraform does not order the binding after the Role. It can be applied before the role exists.

The RoleBinding's role_ref.name is local.emr_service_name instead of a reference to kubernetes_role.emr_containers, so Terraform does not order the binding after the Role. It can be applied before the role exists.

When Windows support is enabled, the ASG launches Windows nodes using the node IAM role, but it does not depend on the eks_windows_cni policy attachment. Nodes can launch before the role has the required Windows CNI EC2 permissions; add aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.eks_windows_cni to the ASG's depends_on.
